subject: science
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Name the organs of the circulatory system: heart, arteries and veins
Draw and label the circulatory organs, and find them on a body cut-out
Describe the work of each organ and the circulation of blood in simple terms
Tell arteries and veins apart, and name a few major ones
Explain the functions of blood
Practise yoga and deep breathing to keep the heart healthy
Name the major bones: skull, jawbone, backbone, chest bone, arm and leg bones
Describe the work of the major bones
Locate the main joints, such as the shoulder, elbow and knee, and say how they work
Name other kinds of joints in the body
Name calcium-rich foods that keep bones strong
Do simple exercises and practise good posture when sitting and standing
Name the components of a balanced diet and explain why it matters
Sort healthy food from junk food
Explain the harm that junk food can do
Suggest ways to make a diet healthier, such as sprouting and fermented foods
Name deficiency diseases, such as night blindness, rickets, scurvy and goitre, and ways to prevent them
Name lifestyle diseases, such as obesity, anaemia, diabetes and blood pressure, and ways to avoid them
Know, at an awareness level, that food can be adulterated
Name the parts of a flower and draw them
Locate the parts of a flower that take part in pollination
Explain pollination in simple technical terms
Tell self-pollination from cross-pollination, with examples
Tell bisexual flowers from unisexual flowers
Explain why plants need pollination
Draw and label the male and female parts of a flower
Explain fertilisation and how a seed forms
Explain sexual and vegetative reproduction, with examples such as potato, ginger, carrot and Bryophyllum
Name the ways seeds spread: by air, by water and by animals
Explain why seed dispersal matters
Carry out simple experiments on seed germination
Describe the properties of solids, such as a definite shape
Describe the properties of liquids: they take the shape of their container and flow
Describe the properties of gases: they have no definite shape or volume
Show the composition of air in a diagram
Explain land and sea breezes and monsoon winds in simple terms
Explain why ventilators, windows and fans are useful in houses
Separate solids from liquids by sedimentation, decantation and filtration

topics.topic: Interdependence in Living Beings: Plants and Animals
covers: Explain that plants make their own food, so they are producers
Explain that animals depend on plants and other animals, so they are consumers
Classify living things as producers and consumers, with examples
Explain a simple food chain using examples from daily life
Name decomposers and scavengers, with examples
Explain how hunting and forest fires upset the balance of nature
Make a model of a food chain
Tell pleasant sounds from unpleasant sounds
Recognise sounds made by common objects, animals, trees and fallen leaves
Explain the difference between sound and noise
Name warning sounds, such as a fire alarm or an ambulance siren, and why they save lives
List the causes of noise pollution and ways to reduce noise
Explain how loud sound can harm health
Explain what work is, with examples from daily life
Tell when work is done and when it is not
Explain why energy is needed to do work
Tell work and energy apart, with examples
Name renewable and non-renewable sources of energy
Name the forms of energy: light, heat, electricity and sound
Explain why energy should be saved
Classify objects as transparent, translucent or opaque
Form shadows, and infer what conditions are needed for them
Describe how the sun seems to change from morning to evening, without looking straight at it
Explain in simple terms why day and night happen
Tell rotation and revolution of the earth apart, in simple words
Explain solar and lunar eclipses in simple language
Name tools and simple machines used in daily life, such as the lever, screw and pulley
Explain the three classes of levers (I, II and III), with examples
Relate body joints, such as the elbow and knee, to levers
Draw and label different machines
Make simple models and show how a machine works
Show when and how to wash their hands properly
Identify diseases that come from unclean surroundings and poor personal hygiene
Sort garbage into degradable and non-degradable, with examples
Suggest ways to reduce non-degradable garbage
Dispose of garbage properly, and make slogans to spread awareness
Share cleanliness and hygiene habits with their family

gaps: Day and night are explained here only in simple terms; the detail is left to Social Studies and Geography.
